cleanIntro: ⛔ This is a clearing and care guide, not a field strip. MasterPiece Arms publishes the DS9 teardown and its cleaning and lubrication instructions only as videos and prints no words for either, so there is no teardown here and none has been invented. What follows is what the DS9 Series owner's manual does write down: how to get the magazine out, clear the chamber and drop the hammer, and the care rules it states.

steps.title: Magazine out FIRST, then look in the chamber
steps.action: The order matters and the manual states it as a rule: the magazine comes out before the slide is touched. Rack the slide with a loaded magazine still seated and you have just chambered the next round, which is the opposite of what you meant to do. Only once the magazine is out do you pull the slide back and look.
steps.quote: When unloading this pistol remove the magazine and only after the magazine has been removed pull back the bolt to visually check to verify that the chamber is empty.
steps.cite: Masterpiece Arms DS9 Series Owner’s Manual — DS9-Manual-3-21 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Safety warnings, PDF p.3 (the book prints no page numbers)

steps.title: Thumb safety UP, then drop the magazine into your hand
steps.action: Push the thumb safety up to SAFE; it works from either side. Hold the pistol in your shooting hand with your other hand cupped under the grip, then press the magazine release all the way in. The magazine should fall free into your palm. If it drags or has to be pulled, check the magazine for damage before it goes back in the gun.
steps.quote: Fully depress the magazine release. The magazine should slide out of the handgun freely.
steps.cite: Masterpiece Arms DS9 Series Owner’s Manual — DS9-Manual-3-21 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Removing the Magazine, PDF p.8

steps.title: Safety off to work the slide, so the finger stays out
steps.action: The thumb safety locks the slide, so the DS9 cannot be racked on SAFE. To clear it you have to move the safety down to FIRE, and from that moment the pistol can fire. That is why the manual pairs the two sentences. Muzzle somewhere safe, finger straight along the frame and outside the guard until the chamber has been seen empty.
steps.quote: The Thumb Safety must be in the READY or FIRE position and the handgun is capable of firing a round. Your finger must be off the trigger and outside of the trigger guard until you confirm the ammunition magazine is removed and the chamber is empty.
steps.cite: Masterpiece Arms DS9 Series Owner’s Manual — DS9-Manual-3-21 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Clearing the Handgun, PDF p.8

steps.title: Slide back and slide stop UP, so the chamber stays open
steps.action: Pull the slide fully to the rear and push the slide stop up to lock it there. A round in the chamber should be thrown out of the ejection port as the slide opens, so let it fall rather than trying to catch it over the port. With the slide locked back you can see into the chamber and the magazine well together.
steps.quote: release and remove the ammunition magazine, pull the slide back and move the slide stop UP to keep the chamber open. If there was a round in the chamber it should eject with the opening of the slide.
steps.cite: Masterpiece Arms DS9 Series Owner’s Manual — DS9-Manual-3-21 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Clearing the Handgun, PDF p.8

steps.title: Look into the chamber, and pick up the round that came out
steps.action: Look into the chamber and the magazine well. If a round is still in the chamber, take it out carefully. Then find the one that was ejected and put both in a container, away from the pistol. A loose round on the bench is how a cleared pistol gets loaded again later.
steps.quote: Inspect the chamber. If there is a round in the chamber, carefully remove it and place it in a appropriate storage container.
steps.cite: Masterpiece Arms DS9 Series Owner’s Manual — DS9-Manual-3-21 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Clearing the Handgun, PDF p.8

steps.title: Close the slide slowly, only after the chamber was seen empty
steps.action: Press the slide stop down and ride the slide forward by hand. The manual makes the order a condition: magazine out and chamber seen empty first. If either is unconfirmed, go back a step rather than closing the slide on it.
steps.quote: Release the slide stop and slowly close the slide only after confirming the ammunition magazine is removed and the chamber is empty.
steps.cite: Masterpiece Arms DS9 Series Owner’s Manual — DS9-Manual-3-21 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Clearing the Handgun, PDF p.8

steps.title: Drop the hammer, muzzle still safe
steps.action: Racking the slide cocked the hammer. With the muzzle still pointed somewhere safe, press the trigger to let the hammer fall. Do this only once the magazine is out and the chamber has been seen empty. The pistol then sits hammer down on an empty chamber, the condition the manual asks for when it is carried or stored.
steps.quote: With the muzzle pointed away from yourself and in a safe direction, depress the trigger to release the hammer.
steps.cite: Masterpiece Arms DS9 Series Owner’s Manual — DS9-Manual-3-21 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Clearing the Handgun, PDF p.8

steps.title: ⛔ The teardown is not published in words, and this guide stops here
steps.action: This is where a field strip would go, and there is not one. The DS9 Series owner's manual has a Disassembly heading and one sentence under it, sending the owner to a video. Nothing in this guide is taken from that video, because a video cannot be quoted or checked. For the teardown itself, use MasterPiece Arms' own video or contact MasterPiece Arms, whose address and phone number are on the front of the manual.
steps.quote: For Disassembly Instructions, please visit the Masterpiece Arms Channel on YouTube for an instruction video on how to Disassemble and Reassemble your DS9 Pistol.
steps.cite: Masterpiece Arms DS9 Series Owner’s Manual — DS9-Manual-3-21 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Handgun Maintenance: Disassembly, PDF p.10

deepAbsentReason: The DS9 Series owner's manual prints no disassembly and no cleaning procedure. Its Disassembly section (PDF p.10) is one sentence referring the owner to a video on the Masterpiece Arms YouTube channel, and its cleaning and lubricating instructions are likewise referred to a Cleaning and Lubrication Video (PDF p.6). The only procedure the book prints in text is unloading and clearing (PDF p.8). A video cannot be quoted or checked, so there is no deep lane.

cleaning.name: BEFORE YOU START
tasks: Clean only a pistol you have just cleared: magazine out, chamber seen empty, hammer down
Keep ammunition off the bench while you work

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Look through the bore before the pistol is loaded again. Congealed oil and grease left in the bore count as an obstruction, not just debris

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Keep lubricant off ammunition, because oil on a cartridge can cause a misfire

cleaning.name: PARTS
tasks: Replace parts only with genuine MasterPiece Arms parts. The DS9 is built to tolerances that need them, and alterations void the warranty

reassembly: ⛔ Nothing was taken apart in this guide, so there is nothing to reassemble. MasterPiece Arms publishes the DS9 teardown and reassembly only as a video.
Leave the pistol hammer down on an empty chamber, and store the magazine and ammunition separately from it.
fncheck: With the pistol cleared (magazine out, chamber seen empty): rack the slide to cock the hammer. Push the thumb safety up to SAFE from one side, then the other, since it is ambidextrous. On SAFE the slide must not move and pressing the trigger must not drop the hammer. The thumb safety goes up only with the hammer cocked. Move it down to FIRE, point the muzzle somewhere safe and press the trigger, and the hammer must fall. If your pistol has a grip safety, cock it again and press the trigger without squeezing the grip safety in: the hammer must stay back. Any other result means the pistol goes back to MasterPiece Arms before it is loaded.
